documents.summary: A 2023 teaching-center post for instructors that recommends a syllabus statement tying unauthorized or uncited AI use to academic misconduct and suggests assignment redesigns. It also points to detectors, with a caution about Turnitin, and to faculty learning events. It sets no AI rule for courses itself.
documents.stance_why: The post only 'recommends that all faculty include a statement on their syllabus' and suggests strategies; it never allows or bans AI for any work and leaves course rules to instructors, so the stance is delegates.

units.fit_note: The recommendation is non-binding ('recommends'), and the statement's content is that misrepresenting AI work is misconduct.

documents.summary: A student-facing guide with a six-level scale of AI use, each level with a description, disclosure standard and examples. Instructors choose the level per assignment. It requires APA citation at Levels 3 and 4 and treats undisclosed required AI use as academic misconduct.
documents.stance_why: The guide offers a tiered scale and says 'Instructors will communicate the level of AI use permitted for each assignment' and 'may set different AI use levels for different assignments', so it sets no stance itself and lists tiers: delegates.

units.why: 'Instructors will communicate the level of AI use permitted for each assignment' says the AI level is set by each instructor per assignment and told to students, a rule about who decides, so P04. It also tells instructors to communicate it, which is why the phase is course-start.
units.anchor: Instructors will communicate the level of AI use permitted for each assignment.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed: policy_type A=P09 B=P04. A coded P09 (AI statement in every syllabus), B coded P04. The source says nothing about a syllabus statement here; it says each instructor communicates the permitted level for each assignment, so the unit is the delegation of the rule to the instructor and assignment: P04 (B). The communication duty is recorded in the why and the phase.

notes: Reconciled 2026-10-26. Four documents coded (utah-1 CTE 2023 post, utah-2 AI & You Student Guide, utah-3 CTE AI Tools for Education, utah-4 ECE page); all stance delegates, which both coders agreed on. Dropped: (a) utah-1, A's second unit on 'without citation, documentation, or authorization' (same sentence as the misconduct unit, and the citation duty is only an inference from it); (b) utah-2, B's separate 'AI is a thought partner / explain concepts' unit (already covered by A's Level 2 permission unit and its fit note); (c) utah-4, A's four plagiarism and misconduct-reporting units (P36 definition and three P81 reporting lines), which are general misconduct procedure on a 'Plagiarism and AI' page and are not about AI. Repeated sentences across CTE pages are coded again in each document, per both coders. unit_stance for citation, disclosure, log and format duties (P24 to P27, modality must or should) is require, following the earlier reconciliation precedent. The school and course layers and the Kahlert School of Computing were not coded (none found or deferred; coder B reported the Kahlert pages had no AI text). No new types; no UNCOVERED units; fit notes from both coders are kept (a note from the coder whose type was not chosen is prefixed with that coder and type).
